# Await every tool call; arguments are keyword-only and omitted optional arguments default to None. Nested object arguments are plain dicts.
# ToolResult = {ok: bool, data: the tool's structured result or None, text: str, files: list[{path: str, line1: int, line2: int, content: str}], diffs: list[dict], images: list[{image: str, index: int}], images_dropped: int, error: str | None, truncated: bool}. Check ok and truncated.
# Constants: PROJECT_ROOT, CHAT_ID, WORKSPACE_DIR, ARTIFACTS_DIR, RUNS_DIR, RUN_ID, RUN_DIR: str; PARENT_ARTIFACTS_DIR: str | None (None without a parent or when the parent has no Python workspace yet).
def help(name: str | None = None) -> str: ...  # one function's full typed signature, parameter docs and data types; no name: the function index
def tools() -> list[str]: ...
def host_path(p: str) -> str: ...
def virtual_path(p: str) -> str: ...
def read(path: str, start: int = 1, end: int | None = None, *, numbered: bool = True) -> str: ...  # lines start..end of a text file (1-based, inclusive; start=-N: last N lines) as "  12 | text"; numbered=False: the exact text
def grep(pattern: str, path: str = ".", *, context: int = 0, glob: str | None = None, ignore_case: bool = False, limit: int = 200, data: bool = False) -> str | dict: ...  # regex search in a file or directory (search_pattern syntax and ignore rules): "path:line: text" lines
def replace(path: str, old: str, new: str, *, count: int = 1) -> str: ...  # exact-text edit; ValueError unless exactly count matches (0: all, at least one); returns a unified diff
async def git(subcommand: Literal["status", "diff", "log", "show", "branches"], *args, **kwargs) -> ToolResult[dict]: ...  # read-only git data, no shell needed: git("status"), git("diff", rev=None, path=None, staged=False), git("log", n=20, rev=None, path=None), git("show", rev, path=None), git("branches")
async def run(cmd: str, *, timeout: int | None = None, cwd: str | None = None, tail: int = 60) -> RunResult: ...  # runs a build or test command to its end through the shell tool (same approvals and rules). RunResult = {ok: bool, exit_code: int | None, status: str, duration_s: float, tail: str, problems: list[str], log: str | None, truncated: bool, error: str | None}
def show(value: Any, *, kind: Literal["table", "markdown", "bar", "line", "area", "scatter", "pie"] | None = None, title: str | None = None, x: str | None = None, y: str | list[str] | None = None, columns: list[str] | None = None) -> None: ...  # show a table, chart or markdown to the user; you only get a one-line note back
# Monty restricted Python. Imports: annotationlib,asyncio,base64,binascii,bisect,collections,copy,csv,dataclasses,datetime,decimal,fnmatch,functools,hashlib,io,itertools,json,math,os,os.path,pathlib,posixpath,random,re,sys,time,tomllib,typing,unicodedata. Missing: ast,shutil,socket,subprocess,threading,urllib. os, re, json, Path and asyncio are imported before every run. io has StringIO, BytesIO and open only (no TextIOWrapper; newline=None does not translate). Path.relative_to missing; paths are not orderable (sort with key=str); with_suffix/rglob, os.walk and os.path.join/relpath/splitext available (partial CPython APIs). globals() is missing. Bound methods cannot be passed as values (max(d, key=d.get) fails; use key=lambda k: d[k]); calling d.get(k, 0) works. No third-party/network/subprocess. A script can import its own .py files from PROJECT_ROOT (no relative imports, no sys.path).
# Tool functions are async and take keyword arguments: the same arguments as the direct tool of the same name. Each returns ToolResult. name(a, b, …) lists the required arguments; … means optional ones exist. After -> come the keys of data: key? may be missing or None, key[] is a list, key[{…}] a list of dicts, key{…} a dict, {*} arbitrary keys. help("name") prints the full typed signature and data types.
shell(command, description, …) -> {stdout}
